cards.name: Bravo Nantahala Adventure Camp
cards.description: Campers hike, raft the Nantahala River, climb, swim and complete a zipline canopy tour. This four-night outdoor adventure camp serves youth with blindness or low vision.

prices.label: Minimum tuition, depending on ability to pay
Maximum tuition, depending on ability to pay

last_year_registration_opened.text: Registration opens on February 1 and closes on May 1, 2026, or sooner if the camp slots fill up.

financial_aid.text: No camper will be turned away due to lack of funds.

special_needs.text: Bravo Adventure Camp is open to rising 9-12th graders who are blind or visually impaired.

lunch.text: Food will be provided by our outfitters, with cafeteria-style service and an on-site dining room.

transportation.text: We ask families to meet us at camp if possible; if not, give me a ring and we’ll see what we can work out.

cards.review_notes: The camp identifies Wildwater Nantahala's Group Lodge as lodging but does not specify the exact check-in point. The venue publishes 10345 Highway 19 South/74 West for Wildwater Nantahala; its directions also identify lodging facilities across the street. Confirm the lodge/check-in address. The interest form is currently unavailable. Eligibility requires screening, mostly independent self-care and travel, and appropriate verbal communication; the camp cannot accommodate certain behaviors or provide 24-hour nursing care.

cards.name: Bravo Asheville Day Camp
cards.description: Campers walk, hike, splash and paddle in the woods and wilds around Asheville. The day camp serves youth with blindness or low vision.

special_needs.text: Campers are rising K-12 graders with blindness or low vision.
